description: A treasury director must decide whether to terminate an interest-rate swap before a planned debt refinancing and finalize the cash settlement, accounting treatment, and collateral instructions, with input from hedge accounting and counterparty risk.

shared_context.S1: The company has a $25,000,000 pay-fixed, receive-floating interest-rate swap supporting floating-rate debt.
shared_context.S2: The debt is expected to be refinanced in approximately 60 days, and the current swap termination quote requires a $1,800,000 payment.
shared_context.S3: Elena makes the binding treasury decision on whether and how to terminate the swap.
shared_context.S4: Before finalizing a material derivative action, Elena's routine process is to obtain a review from hedge accounting and counterparty risk.

PF1.text: Jonas confirmed in an accounting memo received this morning that terminating the swap before the refinancing requires recognition of exactly $650,000 from accumulated other comprehensive income; he has not yet uploaded the memo to the treasury deal file.

PF2.text: Mira received the latest collateral statement this morning showing that the company holds exactly $1,200,000 of eligible collateral from the swap counterparty, which may be applied against the termination payment under the netting agreement; the statement has not yet been matched in the treasury ledger.

acceptance_conditions: Exactly $1,200,000 of held collateral must be applied to the $1,800,000 termination payment.
The resulting cash settlement must be exactly $600,000.
Exactly $650,000 must be identified for other-comprehensive-income reclassification.
The settlement plan must include both collateral application and accounting reclassification commitments.
The hedge-accounting memo must be cited as justification for the accounting treatment.

decisive_facts.why: Without PF1, the settlement would normally omit a specific other-comprehensive-income reclassification and its accounting commitment; PF1 changes oci_reclassification_usd from 0 or unspecified to exactly 650000.

Without PF2, the full $1,800,000 termination payment would ordinarily be treated as cash and no collateral instruction would be included; PF2 changes collateral_applied_usd to exactly 1200000 and cash_settlement_usd to exactly 600000.
